expl: The province was divided into Parganas or Kasbas. The government offi cial of a Pargana was Amil, who collected revenues. stem: Which one of the following is NOT the characteristic of 'Iqta System'?

options.label: a
options.text: Iqta was a revenue collection system

options.label: b
options.text: Siyasatnama was the source of information for Iqta system

options.label: c
options.text: Revenue from Iqta was directly deposited in Sultan's account

options.label: d
options.text: Muqti was supported to maintain troops out of the revenue collected from Iqta

expl: Iqta system in India was introduced by Iltutmish during Sultanate period. According to this system, the owner of Iqta (Iqtadar or Muqti) was given the responsibility of collecting revenue and taxes in his area. Revenue from Iqta was not directly deposited in Sultan's account, whereas it was used by the Muqti to meet his administrative and military expenditures. Muqti had to maintain troops out of this revenue collected from Iqta for the service of Sultan. Siyasatnama authored by Abu Ali Hasan Ibn Ali Tusi (Nizam-ul-Mulk) is the source of information for primary Iqta system.

expl: In the revenue administration of the Delhi Sultanate, the standard division of territories is accepted as Khalisa and Jagirs (Iqta). Therefore, Assertion (A) is correct. Reason (R) is incorrect, because land under the “direct control of the state” was considered Khalisa, whereas a Jagir was granted to a Mansabdar/Jagirdar as a revenue assignment, and it was not an area under the state’s direct control.

stem: With reference to medieval India, which one of the following is the correct sequence in ascending order in terms of size?
expl: With reference to medieval India, entire empire was divided into Suba (province). 'Subedar' was head of administration of Suba. For better administration, every Suba was divided into smaller units called Sarkar whose head was 'Fauzdar'. Every Sarkar was further divided into 'Pargana' or 'Mahal'. Shiqdar was head of this unit. There were villages under Pargana, which were called 'Mavada' or 'Deeha'. 'Nagla' were small colonies under Mavada. During the reign of Shahjahan another unit was formed between Pargana and Sarkar called 'Chakla' under which a few Parganas came. Hence with reference to medieval India, the correct sequence in ascending order in terms of size is – Pargana-Sarkar-Suba.

stem: Who created the department of Diwan-i-Arz in Delhi Sultanate?
expl: Balban (1266-1286 A.D.) was undoubtedly one of the main architects of the Delhi Sultanate, particularly of its form of government and institutions. He separated Diwan-i-wizarat (Finance Department) and created a new Department Diwan-i-Arz (Military Department). He then reorganised the Diwan-i-Arz and deployed the army in diff erent parts of the kingdom to put down the rebellion.

stem: Which one of the following dynasties saw the heyday of the Wizarat:
expl: Wizarat was an institution recognized by the Islamic administration. Non-Arabic institutions were being repealed, and nomenclature used for Minister for Council under emperor was used as Wizarat. The idea for adopting Wizarat as an institution was inspired by Persia by Abbasi Caliphs. Abbas Fazal-Bin-Ahmad was fi rst Wazir in the reign of Mahmud Ghaznavi, (during Ghaznavid administration) who was accomplished in conducting the administration. The prime minister of state was known as Wazir. He headed the fi nance department called the Diwan-i-Wizarat and had the power not only to supervise the income and expenditure of the state but other departments as well. Tughluq era was the golden period of Indian Muslim Wizarat.

stem: Which medieval king of India introduced the ‘Iqta system’?
expl: Iltutmish fi rst introduced 'Iqta' system in Delhi Sultanate Period. In the Islamic empire of the Caliph, land was granted to army offi cials for limited periods in lieu of a regular wage. The Iqta system was introduced in the 9th century A.D. to relieve the state treasury when insuffi cient tax revenue and little booty from wars made it diffi cult for the government to pay salaries.

stem: Supreme rural offi cials of land revenue in Sultanate period?
expl: During the Sultanate period, Chaudhary played an important role in the traditional social structure. If we delineate traditional social structure, it will have at its top the Sultan followed by Sultan’s governors, a village headman who happened to be Chaudhary. Hence, Chaudhary was the main revenue collector for villages during the Sultanate period.

stem: On whose coins the name of the last Caliph of Baghdad appeared for the fi rst time?
expl: On the coins of Alauddin Masud Shah (1242-1246 A.D.), the name of the last Caliph of Baghdad appeared for the fi rst time. The last Caliph of Baghdad was Al-Mustasim. He held this position from 1242-58 A.D. The name of Caliph Mustanasir was inscribed on the coins of Iltutmish (served from 1226 to 1242 A.D.)
